claims.claim: Ericsson links radio/network technology to carrier infrastructure and end-user connectivity; AI-native radio capability can improve network resource allocation, but product capability only becomes a durable bottleneck position through scaled operator adoption and economic contribution.
Q1 organic growth led by Networks supports current demand, while restructuring charges show that cost adaptation remains part of the path from technology capability to durable economics.

risks.risk: Competing radio architectures and vendors can substitute if product advantages do not translate into operator economics.

unknowns.unknown: Full Q2 operating detail and scaled customer economics for AI-native radios are not established by the reused evidence.

claims.claim: AI-native radio announcements are evidence of product execution, not proof of durable incremental economics; scaled deployment and margin contribution remain the relevant falsification tests.
Restructuring and currency effects can obscure underlying operating improvement, so reported and organic trends should remain separated in downstream underwriting.

risks.risk: Product narrative can outrun adoption evidence if AI positioning is treated as economic proof before deployments scale.
Currency and restructuring effects complicate inference from headline profitability.

unknowns.unknown: Full Q2 exhibit metrics were not source-addressed in the inherited Scout pass, limiting current-period falsification strength.
